# Multiply the raw gradient by 1/T_i to counteract transmittance decay [S1]

The evidence explicitly states in Section 3.4 and Appendix A that to counteract the exponential decay of transmittance (which causes samples far from the camera to receive smaller gradients), the method proposes scaling the gradients of the SH coefficients by the reciprocal of transmittance ($1/T_i$). Specifically, the text notes: 'we replace ∇k L_MSE with sTi_k × ∇k L_MSE where sTi_k = Ti^−1' and 'Multiply the gradient of the SH coefficients for that sample by 1/T_i'. This directly supports the claim that the raw gradient is multiplied by 1/T_i to counteract transmittance decay.
